ucs.title: [LLM] APT33 (Peach Sandstorm) password-spray → first-success-from-spray-IP fan-out
ucs.description: Detects APT33's signature initial-access pattern: high-volume low-velocity password spraying against M365 / Entra ID, followed by a *successful* sign-in from the same source IP for one of the sprayed accounts. Microsoft (MSTIC) attributed thousands of this exact spray pattern to Peach Sandstorm in 2023 against defense, satellite, and pharma tenants.
ucs.splunk:
| tstats summariesonly=true count as failed_count from datamodel=Authentication.Authentication where Authentication.action="failure" Authentication.signature_id IN ("50053","50126","50055","50056","50064") earliest=-7d by Authentication.src, Authentication.user, _time span=1h
| stats dc(Authentication.user) as sprayed_users, sum(failed_count) as failed_attempts, min(_time) as spray_start, max(_time) as spray_end by Authentication.src
| where sprayed_users >= 10 AND failed_attempts >= 25
| join type=inner Authentication.src 
  [| tstats summariesonly=true count from datamodel=Authentication.Authentication where Authentication.action="success" earliest=-7d by Authentication.src, Authentication.user, Authentication.app, _time 
  | rename Authentication.* as *]
| where _time >= spray_start AND _time <= (spray_end + 21600)
| eval delta_min = round((_time - spray_end)/60,1)
| table _time, user, src, app, sprayed_users, failed_attempts, delta_min
| sort - _time
ucs.kql:
let SprayWindow = 1h;
let PostSprayPivot = 6h;
let FailedCodes = dynamic([50053, 50055, 50056, 50064, 50126]);  // lockout, expired, bad password, password change required
let Sprays = AADSignInEventsBeta
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where ErrorCode in (FailedCodes)
    | summarize SprayedUsers = dcount(AccountUpn),
                FailedAttempts = count(),
                SprayStart = min(Timestamp),
                SprayEnd   = max(Timestamp)
                by IPAddress, bin(Timestamp, SprayWindow)
    | where SprayedUsers >= 10 and FailedAttempts >= 25;          // empirical APT33 spray-burst floor
let Successes = AADSignInEventsBeta
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where ErrorCode == 0
    | where isnotempty(AccountUpn);
Successes
| join kind=inner Sprays on IPAddress
| where Timestamp between (SprayStart .. SprayEnd + PostSprayPivot)
| extend DelayMin = datetime_diff('minute', Timestamp, SprayEnd)
| project Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Country, City, Application,
          AppDisplayName, ResourceDisplayName, ClientAppUsed, UserAgent,
          SprayedUsers, FailedAttempts, DelayMin, RiskLevelDuringSignIn
| order by Timestamp desc
ucs.sentinel_kql:
let SprayWindow = 1h;
let PostSprayPivot = 6h;
let FailedCodes = dynamic([50053, 50055, 50056, 50064, 50126]);
let Sprays = SigninLogs
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where ResultType in (FailedCodes)
    | summarize SprayedUsers = dcount(UserPrincipalName),
                FailedAttempts = count(),
                SprayStart = min(TimeGenerated),
                SprayEnd   = max(TimeGenerated)
                by IPAddress, bin(TimeGenerated, SprayWindow)
    | where SprayedUsers >= 10 and FailedAttempts >= 25;
let Successes = SigninLogs
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where ResultType == 0
    | where isnotempty(UserPrincipalName);
Successes
| join kind=inner Sprays on IPAddress
| where TimeGenerated between (SprayStart .. SprayEnd + PostSprayPivot)
| extend DelayMin = datetime_diff('minute', TimeGenerated, SprayEnd)
| extend GeoCountry = tostring(parse_json(tostring(LocationDetails)).countryOrRegion)
| project TimeGenerated, UserPrincipalName, IPAddress, GeoCountry, AppDisplayName,
          ResourceDisplayName, ClientAppUsed, UserAgent, AutonomousSystemNumber,
          SprayedUsers, FailedAttempts, DelayMin, RiskLevelDuringSignIn
| order by TimeGenerated desc
ucs.datadog_query: source:azure.activeDirectory @evt.name:"Sign-in activity" @properties.status.errorCode:(50053 OR 50055 OR 50056 OR 50064 OR 50126) -@user.userPrincipalName:(*svc-* OR *_sync* OR *test*)
ucs.falcon_logscale_query:
#event_simpleName=IdpAuthenticationLog AuthenticationResult=/failure/i ReasonForFailure=/(invalid_password|account_locked|password_expired)/i
| groupBy([ClientIP], function=[count(field=UserPrincipal, distinct=true, as=SprayedUsers), count(as=FailedAttempts), min(@timestamp, as=SprayStart), max(@timestamp, as=SprayEnd)])
| SprayedUsers >= 10 AND FailedAttempts >= 25
| join({#event_simpleName=IdpAuthenticationLog AuthenticationResult=/success/i}, field=ClientIP, include=[UserPrincipal, @timestamp])
ucs.rationale: APT33 / Peach Sandstorm's 2023 campaign (MSTIC threat brief, Sep 2023) is defined by exactly this pattern — spray ≥10 accounts from one IP/ASN, then within hours pivot back on the *one* that auths. Hostile-state actors with cloud-first tradecraft (FANCY BEAR, MIDNIGHT BLIZZARD) overlap on the spray TTP, but APT33's distinguishing signature is the *short delay* (typically <1h) between last failure

ucs.title: [LLM] APT33 HTA-borne dropper: mshta.exe → encoded PowerShell (TURNEDUP / POWERTON / FalseFont chain)
ucs.description: Catches APT33's long-standing HTA execution chain documented since 2017 (DROPSHOT/SHAPESHIFT) and still observed in 2023-2024 Peach Sandstorm intrusions: a spear-phished .hta is opened via mshta.exe which spawns PowerShell with -EncodedCommand or a Net.WebClient downloader to fetch the next-stage POWERTON / FalseFont implant.
ucs.splunk:
| tstats summariesonly=true count from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name="mshta.exe" Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe") earliest=-7d by _time, Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process, Processes.parent_process_id, Processes.process, Processes.process_id, Processes.process_hash
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| where match(process, "(?i)(-e(nc(odedcommand)?)?\s+[A-Za-z0-9+/=]{20,}|downloadstring|invoke-expression|\biex\b|frombase64string|net\.webclient|webrequest|hidden|nop|noprofile|bypass)")
| rex field=process "(?i)-e(?:nc(?:odedcommand)?)?\s+(?<b64>[A-Za-z0-9+/=]{20,})"
| eval decoded=if(isnotnull(b64), base64decode(b64), "")
| table _time, dest, user, parent_process, process, decoded, process_hash
| sort - _time
ucs.kql:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "mshta.exe"
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe", "pwsh.exe", "cmd.exe", "wscript.exe", "cscript.exe", "rundll32.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(-e(nc(odedcommand)?)?\s+[A-Za-z0-9+/=]{20,}|downloadstring|invoke-expression|\biex\b|frombase64string|net\.webclient|webrequest|-w\s+hidden|-nop|-noprofile|-bypass)"
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any (".hta", "javascript:", "vbscript:", "http://", "https://")
| extend B64 = extract(@"(?i)-e(?:nc(?:odedcommand)?)?\s+([A-Za-z0-9+/=]{20,})", 1, ProcessCommandLine)
| extend Decoded = iff(isnotempty(B64), base64_decode_tostring(B64), "")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd   = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildImage  = FolderPath,
          ChildCmd    = ProcessCommandLine,
          Decoded, SHA256, MD5
| order by Timestamp desc
ucs.sentinel_kql:
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith @"\mshta.exe"
| where NewProcessName endswith @"\powershell.exe"
    or NewProcessName endswith @"\pwsh.exe"
    or NewProcessName endswith @"\cmd.exe"
    or NewProcessName endswith @"\wscript.exe"
    or NewProcessName endswith @"\cscript.exe"
| where CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(-e(nc(odedcommand)?)?\s+[A-Za-z0-9+/=]{20,}|downloadstring|invoke-expression|\biex\b|frombase64string|net\.webclient|webrequest|-w\s+hidden|-nop|-noprofile|-bypass)"
| where SubjectUserName !endswith "$"
| extend B64 = extract(@"(?i)-e(?:nc(?:odedcommand)?)?\s+([A-Za-z0-9+/=]{20,})", 1, CommandLine)
| extend Decoded = iff(isnotempty(B64), base64_decode_tostring(B64), "")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName,
          CommandLine, Decoded, NewProcessId, ProcessId
| order by TimeGenerated desc
ucs.sigma_yaml:
title: APT33 / Peach Sandstorm HTA Dropper - mshta.exe Spawning Encoded PowerShell
id: 7d3a9e21-4f8c-4b6a-91f2-e8b5d7c93a14
status: experimental
description: Detects APT33's signature execution chain where a spearphished .hta executed by mshta.exe spawns powershell.exe / cmd.exe / cscript.exe with EncodedCommand, base64, or in-memory downloader stubs. Matches TURNEDUP, DROPSHOT (SHAPESHIFT), POWERTON, and FalseFont droppers attributed to G0064 / Refined Kitten / Holmium / Peach Sandstorm.
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0064/
  - https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2023/09/14/peach-sandstorm-password-spray-campaigns-enable-intelligence-collection-at-high-value-targets/
  - https://www.mandiant.com/resources/blog/apt33-insights-into-iranian-cyber-espionage
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/04
tags:
  - attack.execution
  - attack.defense_evasion
  - attack.t1218.005
  - attack.t1059.001
  - attack.t1027
  - attack.g0064
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith: '\mshta.exe'
  selection_child:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
      - '\cmd.exe'
      - '\wscript.exe'
      - '\cscript.exe'
      - '\rundll32.exe'
  selection_cmdline:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '-EncodedCommand'
      - '-enc '
      - '-ec '
      - 'DownloadString'
      - 'Invoke-Expression'
      - 'IEX('
      - 'FromBase64String'
      - 'Net.WebClient'
      - 'WebRequest'
      - '-w hidden'
      - '-nop'
      - '-noprofile'
      - '-bypass'
  condition: selection_parent and selection_child and selection_cmdline
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate enterprise software that ships HTA-driven installers spawning PowerShell (rare; investigate)
level: high
ucs.datadog_query: source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @ParentImage:(*\\mshta.exe OR *\\MSHTA.EXE OR *\\Mshta.exe) @Image:(*\\powershell.exe OR *\\PowerShell.exe OR *\\POWERSHELL.EXE OR *\\pwsh.exe OR *\\cmd.exe OR *\\wscript.exe OR *\\cscript.exe) @CommandLine:(*EncodedCommand* OR *-enc* OR *DownloadString* OR *Invoke-Expression* OR *IEX(* OR *FromBase64String* OR *Net.WebClient* OR *-nop* OR *-noprofile* OR *bypass*)
ucs.falcon_logscale_query:
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/mshta\.exe$/i
| ImageFileName=/(powershell|pwsh|cmd|wscript|cscript|rundll32)\.exe$/i
| regex("(?i)(-e(nc(odedcommand)?)?\\s+[A-Za-z0-9+/=]{20,}|downloadstring|invoke-expression|\\biex\\b|frombase64string|net\\.webclient|webrequest|-w\\s+hidden|-nop|-noprofile|-bypass)", field=CommandLine)
| NOT UserName=/\$$/
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ParentBaseFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, SHA256HashData], function=[min(@timestamp, as=FirstSeen), count(as=Hits)])
| sort(FirstSeen, order=desc)
ucs.rationale: The mshta → powershell chain is APT33's most durable code-execution fingerprint across a decade. Mandiant's 2017 APT33 report flagged it for DROPSHOT/SHAPESHIFT, FireEye documented it for TURNEDUP/POWERTON in 2018, and MSTIC's 2023 Peach Sandstorm brief shows the same parent-child pair still driving FalseFont droppers. The combination is high-fidelity because legitimate mshta usage is rare on work
